info.title: PayAI x402 Facilitator API
info.summary: Verify and settle x402 micropayments across Solana and EVM networks, and browse the PayAI Bazaar catalog of x402-payable resources.
info.description:
The PayAI Facilitator implements the facilitator role of the [x402 protocol](https://docs.payai.network/x402/introduction): it verifies signed payment payloads and settles them on-chain so a resource server never has to touch a wallet, an RPC node, or a private key.

**When an agent should call this API**

- You received an HTTP `402 Payment Required` response with x402 payment requirements and need to know whether a signed payment is valid before serving a resource — call `POST /verify`.
- You have verified a payment and want the funds moved on-chain — call `POST /settle`.
- You need to know which chains, schemes, and x402 versions are live right now — call `GET /supported`.
- You want to discover x402-payable APIs, MCP tools, and services that accept agent payments — call `GET /discovery/resources`.

**Authentication.** `GET` endpoints are public and unauthenticated. `POST /verify` and `POST /settle` accept an optional `Authorization: Bearer <api-key>` for credit accounting, per-account rate lanes, and analytics attribution; without a key, requests are served on the free tier. Create a key in the [merchant portal](https://merchant.payai.network).

**Error shape.** Errors are JSON, never HTML. `/verify` failures return `{ isValid: false, invalidReason, invalidMessage }`; `/settle` failures return `{ success: false, errorReason, errorMessage, transaction, network, payer }`. The `x402` client SDKs expect this shape on non-2xx responses too, so an error body is always parseable.

**Versioning.** The facilitator is versioned by the x402 protocol version it speaks, not by a URL path segment and not by a version request header. There is no `/v1/` prefix and requesting one returns 404. Every request carries `x402Version` (1 or 2) in its body, and `GET /supported` advertises which (version, scheme, network) combinations are live — v1 uses short network names (`base`), v2 uses CAIP-2 identifiers (`eip155:8453`). Both versions are served from the same endpoints, so an integration pins a version by what it sends, not by what it calls.

**Deprecation.** A payment kind is withdrawn by disappearing from `GET /supported` before the endpoints stop accepting it, so a client that checks `/supported` sees a removal in advance. Breaking changes to the request or response shapes arrive as a new `x402Version`; existing versions keep working until they are removed from `/supported`.

**Every response is JSON.** `GET /health`, `/supported` and the `/discovery/*` endpoints answer failures with RFC 9457 problem details (`application/problem+json`), as does every unknown path and every unhandled error. Only `/verify` and `/settle` differ, and only because the x402 client SDKs require it: they keep the typed `VerifyResponse` / `SettleResponse` shapes on 4xx and 5xx. No endpoint on this origin returns an HTML error page.

**Rate limits.** Throughput is limited per client IP at the edge, split across three buckets: `/settle`, the payment reads (`/verify`, `/supported`), and everything else including `/discovery/*`. Exceeding a bucket is rejected before the request reaches the API.

Advertised as `RateLimit-Policy` on every response; the policy governing the path you called is `settle` (100 req/s), `payments-read` (200 req/s), `discovery` (25 req/s). The budget is applied per ingress replica, so treat it as a floor rather than an exact ceiling.

No `RateLimit` header reporting *remaining* budget is emitted: the limiter runs at the edge and this API is not told how much of your budget is left. Back off on the response status, not on a header countdown.

Separately from request rate, the free tier is capped by total settlements. Exhausting it returns HTTP 403 with an `errorReason` beginning `free_tier_exhausted`.

Full guides: https://docs.payai.network//x402/quickstart

tags.name: Discovery
tags.description: Browse the PayAI Bazaar: the catalog of resources that accept x402 payments.

get.description: Returns 200 when the facilitator is accepting traffic. Use for uptime monitoring, not for capability discovery — call `getSupportedPaymentKinds` for that.

Returns every (x402 version, scheme, network) combination the facilitator can currently verify and settle. Call this before constructing payment requirements so you only advertise networks that are live. Solana `exact` entries include `extra.feePayer` plus best-effort `recentBlockhash` and decimal-string `lastValidBlockHeight` hints that must not be cached for more than five seconds. Solana `upto` entries include only the static `feePayer`; EVM `upto` entries include `extra.facilitatorAddress`.

parameters.name: Authorization
parameters.description: Optional `Bearer <api-key>`. Read here to steer which settlement lane the advertised Solana fee payer belongs to, so an account with a reserved lane sees its own fee payer. Omit it for the shared lane.

get.description: Self-describing hint for agents that probe with GET. Returns the endpoint name and the expected request body keys. Verification itself requires POST.

post.description: Checks that a signed payment payload satisfies the supplied payment requirements: correct scheme and network, sufficient balance, valid signature, unexpired authorization, and compliance screening. Verification does not move funds — call `settlePayment` for that. A resource server should verify before doing expensive work, then settle before returning the paid resource.

200.description: Verification ran. Inspect `isValid` — a valid *and* an invalid payment can both return 200.

get.description: Self-describing hint for agents that probe with GET. Returns the endpoint name and the expected request body keys. Settlement itself requires POST.

post.summary: Settle a verified x402 payment on-chain
post.description:
Broadcasts the payment on the target network and waits, within a bounded budget, for confirmation. Settlement is idempotent per payment payload: re-submitting the exact same body returns the recorded outcome rather than paying twice.

If confirmation outruns the response budget the facilitator answers with `errorReason: "settlement_pending"` **and** the broadcast `transaction` hash — the payment may still land, so treat this as unresolved, not failed, and re-submit the identical body to poll for the final outcome. A `duplicate_settlement` reason on that poll means the original attempt is still in flight.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Settlement is already idempotent per signed payment payload; this optional header adds standard replay semantics for clients that retry. A key is bound to the first request body it is used with for 24 hours, even while the outcome is unresolved: same-body retries replay a recorded terminal outcome with `Idempotency-Replayed: true`, reuse with a different body returns 422 regardless of outcome state, and concurrent same-body use returns 409. Non-terminal outcomes, including `settlement_pending`, `duplicate_settlement`, 429, and 5xx responses, are never cached, so re-submitting the same body continues polling. Keys and terminal outcomes expire after 24 hours.

200.description: Settlement resolved. Inspect `success`; on failure read `errorReason`.

get.summary: List x402-payable resources in the PayAI Bazaar
get.description: Returns the catalog of resources that accept x402 payments, newest first. Each item carries the payment terms (`accepts`) an agent needs to construct a payment, plus optional `inputSchema`/`outputSchema` for resources that describe themselves well enough to be called as a tool. Use this to answer 'what can I buy with an agent payment right now?'.

get.summary: Get settlement statistics for one catalog resource
get.description: Settlement counts, volume, success rate, and response-time percentiles for a single resource in the PayAI Bazaar. Use it to judge whether a resource an agent is about to pay for is actually being used and actually settles.

parameters.name: resource
parameters.description: The catalog item's `resource` value, URL-encoded. Take it verbatim from `listDiscoveryResources`.

503.description: The statistics cache is being rebuilt. Carries `Retry-After`.

get.summary: Deprecated alias for the Bazaar catalog
get.description: Superseded by `listDiscoveryResources`. Answers 308 with the query string preserved; follow the redirect or call `/discovery/resources` directly.

Returns catalog size, settlement counts over 24h/7d/30d, settlement volume, facilitator uptime, a per-network settlement breakdown, and the busiest merchant hosts. Useful for answering questions about x402 adoption and which networks carry real traffic.

503.description: The statistics cache is being rebuilt. Carries `Retry-After`; retry after the indicated delay.

VerificationError.description: Verification failed. Always JSON — read `invalidReason` for the machine-readable cause.

SettlementError.description: Settlement failed or is unresolved. Always JSON — read `errorReason`.

RateLimited.description: The per-IP edge budget for this path was exceeded. The limiter runs ahead of the API, so the body is the edge's, not a facilitator error shape. Back off and retry; the governing budget is named in the `RateLimit-Policy` response header.

RateLimit-Policy.description: The per-IP policy governing this path, as a structured field: name, quota q, window w in seconds.

Problem.description: RFC 9457 problem details. Never an HTML error page.

bearerApiKey.description: Optional PayAI API key for credit accounting, dedicated rate lanes, and analytics attribution. Create one at https://merchant.payai.network. Omit it to use the free tier.

ResourceStatsResponse.description: Settlement activity and reliability for one catalog resource. Counts are bucketed once they pass a threshold, so small numbers read exactly and large ones are rounded.

resource.description: The catalog resource these figures describe.

reliability.description: Percentage of settlement attempts that succeeded.

uptime.description: Availability of the resource itself, as observed by the facilitator uptime probe.

avgResponseMs.description: Mean probe response time over 24 hours.

networks.description: Settlement count per network, keyed by network name.

cachedAt.description: When these figures were computed. Results are cached briefly.

StatsUnavailable.description: The statistics cache is being rebuilt.

ProblemDetails.description: RFC 9457 problem details. Returned by every endpoint except `/verify` and `/settle`, and by every unknown path, with `Content-Type: application/problem+json`.

type.description: Stable URI identifying the problem kind. Dereferences to documentation for that failure.

title.description: Short, human-readable summary of the problem kind.

status.description: HTTP status code, repeated for clients that only read the body.

detail.description: Human-readable explanation specific to this occurrence.

instance.description: The path that produced the problem, when it is useful to echo it.

FacilitatorError.description: Every failure response carries a stable machine-readable reason code and a human-readable message, and is JSON on 4xx and 5xx as well as on 200. Branch on the reason code; it does not change across releases.

success.description: False on failure. `POST /verify` expresses the same thing as `isValid`.

PaymentPayload.description: A signed x402 payment, produced by an x402 client SDK. The inner `payload` shape is scheme- and chain-specific: EVM `exact` carries an EIP-3009 authorization and signature, Solana `exact` carries a base64 partially-signed transaction.

x402Version.description: x402 protocol version this payload conforms to.

scheme.description: Payment scheme. `exact` charges a fixed amount; `upto` opens a payment channel that settles up to a ceiling.

network.description: Target network. x402 v1 uses short names (`base`, `solana`); v2 uses CAIP-2 identifiers (`eip155:8453`, `solana:5eykt4UsFv8P8NJdTREpY1vzqKqZKvdp`).

payload.description: Scheme- and chain-specific signed payment material.

PaymentRequirements.description: The payment terms a resource server advertises in its HTTP 402 response. The client signs a payment that satisfies these terms.

maxAmountRequired.description: Maximum chargeable amount in the asset's smallest unit, as a decimal string (USDC has 6 decimals, so `10000` is $0.01).

amount.description: Exact amount in the asset's smallest unit, as a decimal string.

payTo.description: Recipient address on the target network.

maxTimeoutSeconds.description: How long the resource server will wait for settlement.

asset.description: Token contract address (EVM) or mint address (Solana) of the payment asset. PayAI settles USDC by default.

extra.description: Scheme-specific extras, e.g. `feePayer` plus short-lived `recentBlockhash` and string `lastValidBlockHeight` hints for Solana `exact`, or `facilitatorAddress` for EVM `upto` channels.

EndpointDescription.description: Self-describing hint returned by GET on a POST-only endpoint.

extra.description: Scheme-specific metadata, e.g. `feePayer` and short-lived blockhash hints (Solana), or `facilitatorAddress` (EVM `upto` channels).

kinds.description: Flat list containing both x402 v1 short network names and v2 CAIP-2 identifiers, for backward compatibility.

VerifyResponse.description: Result of a verification attempt. Always JSON, including on 4xx and 5xx. Satisfies the FacilitatorError contract: `invalidReason` is the stable reason code, `invalidMessage` the human-readable detail.

isValid.description: True only if the payment satisfies the requirements.

invalidReason.description: Stable machine-readable failure code. Present when `isValid` is false.

invalidMessage.description: Human-readable detail, including field-level validation errors.

payer.description: Address that signed the payment, when it could be recovered.

SettleResponse.description: Result of a settlement attempt. Always JSON, including on 4xx and 5xx. Satisfies the FacilitatorError contract: `errorReason` is the stable reason code, `errorMessage` the human-readable detail.

success.description: True only if funds moved and the transaction confirmed.

errorReason.description: Stable machine-readable failure code. `settlement_pending` means the outcome is unresolved, not failed.

errorMessage.description: Human-readable detail, including how to reconcile a pending settlement.

transaction.description: On-chain transaction hash or signature. Empty string when nothing was broadcast; populated on `settlement_pending` so the payment can be reconciled on-chain.

network.description: Network the settlement was attempted on.

payer.description: Address funds were debited from. Empty string when unknown.

DiscoveryItem.description: One x402-payable resource in the Bazaar catalog.

resource.description: URL of the payable resource. May contain `:param` path placeholders.

toolName.description: Tool name for `mcp` resources; null for HTTP.

inputSchema.description: Declared input shape, when the seller published one.

outputSchema.description: Declared output shape, when the seller published one.

lastUpdated.description: When this catalog entry last changed.

DiscoveryStatsResponse.description: Aggregate, cached Bazaar and settlement statistics.

settlements.description: Successful settlement counts. `total` is a rounded display string; the windowed counts are exact integers.

totalUsd.description: Rounded display string for total settled USD volume.

networks.description: Successful settlements keyed by network identifier.
